subject: spanish
promptStrong: Give me a 40-word writing task in Spanish on {lo} for {board} {level} {subject}, then mark my answer for accuracy and range.
promptWeak: Give me a two-way translation drill (Spanish↔English) on {lo} for {board} {level} {subject}, with answers and the common mistakes to avoid.

questions.q: How do you say “I gave up sweets to be healthier”?
options: Dejé de comer dulces para estar más sano
Dejé de comer dulces para estar más enfermo
Empecé a comer dulces para estar más sano
Dejo de comer dulces para estar más sano
questions.explain: “Dejar de” + infinitive = “to give up/stop”, so “Dejé de comer dulces” = “I gave up eating sweets”.

questions.q: Which sentence means 'I went to the cinema yesterday'?
options: Ayer iba al cine a menudo
questions.explain: 'Fui' is the preterite of 'ir' (I went); with 'ayer' the completed past is correct: 'Ayer fui al cine'.

questions.q: How do you say 'I do exercise to keep fit'?
options: Hace ejercicio para mantenerme en forma
Hago ejercicio para mantenerme en forma
Hago ejercicio porque estoy en forma
questions.explain: 'Mantenerse en forma' = 'to keep fit' and 'para' = 'in order to'; 'hago' is the correct first-person form.

questions.q: How would you write 'limpio' to describe two beaches ('playas')?
questions.explain: 'Playa' is feminine, so the plural adjective is feminine plural: 'limpias'.

questions.q: How would you write 'trabajador' to describe a hard-working woman?
questions.explain: Adjectives ending in -dor add -a for the feminine singular, so a hard-working woman is 'trabajadora'.

questions.q: How do you say “You should drink plenty of water”?
questions.explain: “Se debe” = “one should” and “beber” (not “comer”) is used for drinks: “Se debe beber mucha agua”.
'El tabaquismo' is the habit/addiction of smoking, not a shop (that would be 'el estanco').

questions.q: What does 'soy aficionado al baloncesto' mean?
options: I am a fan of basketball
questions.explain: 'Ser aficionado a' means 'to be a fan of', so this means 'I am a fan of basketball'.
“Quedarse” = to stay, so “quedarse en casa” = “to stay at home”.

questions.q: How do you say “I find horror films scary”?
options: La película de terror me dan miedo
Las películas de terror me dan risa
Las películas de terror me dan miedo
Las películas de terror me dan igual
questions.explain: “Dar miedo” = “to frighten”, so “me dan miedo” = “they scare me”.

questions.q: Which sentence means 'You must avoid sugary drinks'?
options: Hay que evitar las bebidas azucaradas
questions.explain: 'Hay que' = 'one must' and 'evitar' = 'to avoid', so 'Hay que evitar las bebidas azucaradas' = 'You must avoid sugary drinks'.
'La Nochebuena' (24 December) means 'Christmas Eve'; 'la Nochevieja' is New Year's Eve.
'La asignatura' is a false friend: it means 'school subject', not 'signature' (which is 'la firma').
“Disfrazarse” means “to dress up / wear a costume”, e.g. at carnival.
